name: sugarcane processing, modern annexed plant | sugar, from sugarcane | Cutoff, U
description:
ecoQuery: https://ecoquery.ecoinvent.org/3.11/cutoff/dataset/21396/documentation

This dataset represents a modern sugarcane mill processing of 4 million metric tonnes of sugarcane stalks per year for the production of raw sugar, ethanol (anhydrous and hydrated) and electricity. The plant operates 200 days per season. ;The industrial process diverts 50% of sugarcane juice for row sugar production and the other 50%, along with molasses (a by-product of sugar crystallization process), is diverted to ethanol production process. Plant configuration includes reduction of overall energy consumption to maximize of electricity output. It considers high-pressure boilers (65 bar, 485°C), application of thermal integration strategies reducing 20% of low-pressure steam demand, electrical drives in the crushing mills and molecular sieves for anhydrous ethanol production. ;Overall process efficiencies assumed were 96% for sugars extraction, 89.5% for ethanol fermentation and 76.5% for sugar recovery as raw sugar. Each 1000 kg of cane stalks yields 51.4 kg of raw sugar, 32.6 L of hydrated ethanol (93% w/w), 22.8 L of anhydrous ethanol (99.6% w/w); and 111.3 kWh of surplus electricity.

This activity starts when sugarcane arrives at the industrial area.

The dataset includes the sugarcane conversion into raw sugar, ethanol and surplus electricity. Processing equipment, chemical inputs, industrial area, water use treatment, and emissions to air are included in the inventory.  Sugarcane processed arrives with 5% of vegetal impurities (sugarcane straw) and 1% of mineral impurities (dirt). No additional sugarcane straw recovery and industrial use is considered.
The activity ends when products are available at factory gate.

It considers high-pressure boilers (22 bar, 300°C), mechanical drives in the crushing mills and azeotropic distillation for anhydrous ethanol production. ;Overall process efficiencies assumed were 96% for sugars extraction, 90% for ethanol fermentation and 76.5% for sugar recovery as raw sugar. Each 1000 kg of cane stalks yields 51.3 kg of raw sugar, 32.3 L of hydrated ethanol (93% w/w), 23.0 L of anhydrous ethanol (99.6% w/w); 6.0 kWh of surplus electricity; and 81.8 kg of surplus bagasse (50% moisture).

name: hydrated lime production, loose | hydrated lime, loose | Cutoff, U
description:
ecoQuery: https://ecoquery.ecoinvent.org/3.11/cutoff/dataset/11764/documentation

This dataset represents the production of hydrated lime in Quebec (Canada), from quicklime in pieces.;Hydrated lime is used in a variety of industrial applications including water treatment, as an anti-stripping agent in asphalt, and in soil stabilization. Some hydrated limes are sold into the food grade market as well.;Hydrated lime Ca(OH)2 is a dry powder produced by reacting quicklime with a sufficient amount of water to satisfy the quicklime's natural affinity for moisture. The process converts CaO to Ca(OH)2. The amount of water required depends on both the subtle characteristics of the quicklime and the type of hydrating equipment available. Hydrated lime easily forms as a suspension or slurry and is often pumped to various process locations within industrial plants. The resulting solution is strongly alkaline, having a pH of 12.4. Most hydrated limes contain approximately 75 percent CaO and 25 percent H2O.;Electricity and water consumption were provided by the only hydrated lime producer in Quebec. A weighted average of their two (2) hydrated lime plants is used.;Infrastructure data was extrapolated from "lime production, hydrated, loose weight, GLO 2000-2002" ecoinvent dataset: The value of the infrastructure is normalized with a annual production capacity of about 20'000 tons of product per year. The estimated lifespan of the machines is 25 years. There are no significant dust emissions as a dust control system is installed.

From the reception of quicklime in pieces at the factory gate.

This activity ends with the hydrated lime, loose, at the plant gate.

This dataset includes the processes: slaking, crushing, dust abatement (cyclone), transportation and storing. A part of the total heating energy for "production" and "administration" is included. Equipment included in the infrastructure: 1 swing hammer crusher, 2 cyclone dust catchers, 1 lime slaking plant, 2 conveyor worms, and 1 silo.
